# Zoom and reflow

> Status: AI-drafted, not human-reviewed

Group id: `zoom-reflow`. Change the size and presentation of the page and see what breaks: 200% zoom, 320 CSS px width, the text-spacing override, portrait and landscape, and content that appears on hover or focus. Each state is rendered by script; judging compares it with the 100% render.

## Setup

- Chromium at 1280 x 1024 at 100% as the baseline. Zoom is browser zoom, which changes the CSS viewport: 200% gives a 640 x 512 CSS px viewport, 400% a 320 x 256 one. Use DevTools Protocol `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` with width 640 / 320 and device scale factor 2 / 4, or real browser zoom.
- Text spacing: inject one stylesheet that sets, with `!important`, on `*`: `line-height: 1.5`, `letter-spacing: 0.12em`, `word-spacing: 0.16em`, and on `p`: `margin-bottom: 2em` (the four values in WCAG 1.4.12; the numbers are relative to the font size). Do not change the font size.
- Orientation: 390 x 844 (portrait) and 844 x 390 (landscape) with touch emulation.
- Tools: DevTools, or the open text-spacing bookmarklet. AI: a vision-capable model plus the measured numbers below.

## Collect

Collect all of this before judging. Each item names the data type (`needs` key in the data file). A script or a cheap model can do it without judgement; store each artifact with a file name that the report can cite.

1. **zoomed-render** — Baseline at 100%: full-page screenshot; text inventory (every text-owning element: selector, text, bounding box); count of interactive elements; `scrollWidth` and `clientWidth` of the document.
2. **zoomed-render** — Same record at 200% (640 x 512 CSS px). Add: does a horizontal scrollbar exist; elements whose bounding box overlaps another text element's box; elements with `overflow: hidden` whose `scrollWidth` or `scrollHeight` exceeds `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`; text or controls present at 100% that are missing or not visible now (compare inventories).
3. **zoomed-render** — Same record at 400% (320 x 568 CSS px for vertical-scrolling pages; 1280 x 256 CSS px viewport for horizontal-scrolling pages if the page is written in a horizontal script). Add: every element with `getBoundingClientRect().right` greater than 320 and the list of ancestors that scroll, to see what forces horizontal scroll. Screenshot at each vertical scroll step.
4. **text-spacing-render** — At 1280 px: inject the text-spacing stylesheet, screenshot, and record clipped text (container with overflow hidden and `scrollHeight` > `clientHeight`), overlapping boxes, and text or controls no longer visible. Also list inline style declarations containing spacing properties with `!important` (they block the override).
5. **screenshot** — Portrait and landscape renders of the page; the computed CSS in effect at each (`@media (orientation: ...)` rules that hide content, rotate with `transform`, or show a "rotate your device" message).
6. **interaction** — Hover/focus content: list triggers (elements with `mouseover`/`mouseenter`/`focus` handlers revealing content, `:hover`/`:focus` rules that change `display` or `visibility`, tooltips, popovers, `aria-describedby` targets that appear). For each: hover it and screenshot; move the pointer onto the new content and screenshot; move the pointer away and screenshot; with the content shown press Escape and screenshot; focus the trigger by Tab and repeat; wait 5 seconds with the pointer or focus still on the trigger and record whether the content stays.
7. **dom** — For 1.4.8: for each block of body text: characters per line (width of line / average character width), `text-align`, `line-height` / `font-size`, paragraph spacing / line height; search for controls that let the user change foreground and background colour.

## Judge

Count only losses of content or function and clear overlap. A different layout is not a failure.

### 1.3.4 Orientation (AA)

- **Fails when:** Content is restricted to portrait or landscape by CSS (F97) or by a "rotate your device" message that blocks use.
- **Passes when:** Both orientations render and are usable.
- **Common false positives:** Essential cases (a bank cheque, a piano keyboard, a VR application).
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Orientation lock is set in script at run time on a real device.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/orientation.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F97, F100 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA)

- **Fails when:** At 200% zoom text, images or controls are clipped, truncated or obscured (F69); form controls do not resize (F80); the viewport meta tag blocks zoom (`user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale` below 2).
- **Passes when:** All content and function remain available at 200% on a 1280 px wide window.
- **Common false positives:** Captions and images of text are exempt; horizontal scroll at 200% is judged under 1.4.10.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Mild overlap you cannot classify as loss; low confidence.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F69, F80, F94 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.4.8 Visual Presentation (AAA)

- **Fails when:** A mechanism to choose foreground and background colour is missing (F24); lines longer than 80 characters (40 for CJK); body text is justified (F88); line spacing is under 1.5 in paragraphs or paragraph spacing under 1.5 times the line spacing; 200% zoom needs horizontal scrolling.
- **Passes when:** Measured values meet the limits and 200% has no horizontal scroll.
- **Common false positives:** Code blocks and tables; the user agent's own colour settings can count as the mechanism.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Whether a browser-level feature may count as the mechanism.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/visual-presentation.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F24, F88 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.4.10 Reflow (AA)

- **Fails when:** At 320 CSS px width (400%), vertical-scrolling content needs horizontal scrolling, or content or function is lost (F102).
- **Passes when:** Content reflows into one column with no loss and no two-dimensional scrolling.
- **Common false positives:** Exempt: images, maps, diagrams, video, games, presentations, data tables and toolbars that need two-dimensional layout.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** It is unclear whether the exception applies.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F102 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.4.12 Text Spacing (AA)

- **Fails when:** With the text-spacing override, text or controls are clipped, overlap or disappear (F104), or inline `!important` declarations block the override.
- **Passes when:** All text and controls remain visible and usable with the override.
- **Common false positives:** Text in scripts that the override does not apply to; the override changed only some properties.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Borderline overlap or truncation with an ellipsis; low confidence.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F104 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA)

- **Fails when:** Content that appears on hover or focus: cannot be dismissed without moving pointer or focus, disappears when the pointer moves onto it, or disappears by itself before the user dismisses it (F95).
- **Passes when:** It can be dismissed (Escape), hovered over, and stays until the user dismisses it or removes hover or focus.
- **Common false positives:** Native `title` tooltips; error messages and user-controlled content; content that does not obscure other content needs no dismissal.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** You did not find all triggers; list the ones you tested.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F95 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

## Already covered by tools

Our retest showed that axe has no rule for these states, apart from viewport settings that block zoom, an orientation lock written in CSS media queries and inline spacing declarations. HTML_CodeSniffer gives notices or warnings about fixed widths; the 1.4.4 sniff is not part of the WCAG2AAA ruleset.

- **1.3.4** (partial) axe: css-orientation-lock; HTML_CodeSniffer: no sniff. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. axe detects CSS orientation locks in media queries; locks done in script or by the manifest are missed.
- **1.4.4** (partial) axe: meta-viewport; HTML_CodeSniffer: no sniff. Retest (4 failing cases): axe 4 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 missed. axe only catches viewport settings that block zoom; text clipped or overlapping at 200% is not tested. The 1.4.4 sniff is not in the WCAG2AAA ruleset.
- **1.4.8** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_4_8.H87,C20, 1_4_8.C19,G172,G169, 1_4_8.G188,C21. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Notices only, one per requirement; no rule decides line length, justification, spacing or colour selection.
- **1.4.10** (partial) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_4_10.C32,C31,C33,C38,SCR34,G206. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. HTML_CodeSniffer warns about fixed-width elements that may scroll in two dimensions; axe has no rule.
- **1.4.12** (partial) axe: avoid-inline-spacing; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_4_12.C36,C35. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. axe only finds inline !important spacing that blocks overrides; clipping after the override is not tested.
- **1.4.13** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_4_13.F95. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Notice only; dismissable, hoverable and persistent behaviour needs interaction.

## AI and human

Taken from the data file (`ai.level`, `human.level`). Levels: AI likely/possible/unlikely; human must/should/optional.

- **1.3.4** Orientation: AI likely (needs screenshot, interaction); human optional. AI: Rendering in portrait and landscape viewports and comparing is straightforward. Human: Renders in both orientations settle it; the 'essential' exception is rare.
- **1.4.4** Resize Text: AI likely (needs zoomed-render, screenshot); human should. AI: Comparing 100% and 200% renders for clipped, overlapping or missing text is feasible. Human: Overlap and truncation in screenshots are easy to overlook; confirm.
- **1.4.8** Visual Presentation: AI possible (needs dom, screenshot, zoomed-render); human should. AI: Line length, justification and spacing are measurable from computed styles; user colour selection and 200% without horizontal scroll need interaction. Human: Several sub-requirements; confirm.
- **1.4.10** Reflow: AI likely (needs zoomed-render, screenshot, dom); human should. AI: Rendering at 320 CSS px, checking scroll width and comparing content is scriptable. Human: Loss of content or function at 320 px and the 2D-layout exception need confirmation.
- **1.4.12** Text Spacing: AI likely (needs text-spacing-render, screenshot); human should. AI: Comparing renders before and after the text-spacing bookmarklet styles shows clipping and overlap. Human: Confirm clipping found or missed in screenshots.
- **1.4.13** Content on Hover or Focus: AI possible (needs interaction, screenshot); human should. AI: A scripted agent can hover, focus, press Escape and move into the popup, but finding all triggers is error-prone. Human: Confirm with pointer and keyboard.

## Report

Write one finding per criterion and location. Use exactly these fields.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `criterion` | Success criterion id, for example `1.4.3` |
| `outcome` | `failed`, `passed`, `inapplicable` or `cantTell` |
| `location` | Page URL plus CSS selector of the element (or `page` for page-level findings) |
| `evidence` | One to three sentences of fact: what was observed, with numbers where they exist. Name the collected artifact (file name or step number in the trace) |
| `confidence` | `high`, `medium` or `low` |
| `tester` | `human` or the model id of the AI that judged |

Rules:
- `failed` needs evidence that shows the failure; do not write it from a guess.
- `passed` means that this tester checked the criterion across the collected data and found no failure; it is not a conformance claim.
- `inapplicable` means the content the criterion is about does not exist on the page (state which content you looked for).
- `cantTell` means the data cannot decide it. Say what is missing and which pass or person could decide.
- One finding per element and criterion; do not merge different locations.

Example (JSON, one finding):

```json
{"criterion": "2.4.7", "outcome": "failed", "location": "https://example.org/form#nav a.skip", "evidence": "No visible change between focused and blurred crops at focus step 3 (focus-trace/step-03.png): outline is none, no replacement style.", "confidence": "medium", "tester": "claude-sonnet-5-5"}
```
